Root cause: /app/backend/ai/llm.py line 40 calls .with_max_tokens(900) on LlmChat, but emergentintegrations LlmChat does not expose that method -> AttributeError. Pipeline catches only LLMUnavailable so this AttributeError propagates to FastAPI as a 500.

rca of the issue: 1) /app/backend/ai/llm.py line 40 chains .with_max_tokens(900) on the LlmChat builder. Current emergentintegrations build does not expose with_max_tokens (only with_model and the implicit session token). Result: AttributeError on every call. Both regenerate_summary and suggest_reply call call_llm_json directly and catch only LLMUnavailable, so the AttributeError bubbles up to FastAPI and the endpoint returns 500. Spec explicitly requires these endpoints to return 200 with a graceful payload (error: '...') when LLM is unavailable. Fix: either drop .with_max_tokens(900) (server.py default tokens are fine) OR wrap call_llm_json in a broad try/except Exception that maps to LLMUnavailable. 2) send_message in server.py returns msg_doc directly after insert_one — Motor mutates the dict to add an ObjectId _id, then FastAPI's jsonable_encoder fails with TypeError('ObjectId' object is not iterable). Fix: return msg.model_dump() or pop _id before returning. 3) Frontend BotIATab does not perform client-side validation for ctxmax range; the backend correctly returns 400 but the toast surfaced is generic ('No se pudo guardar' or similar), not the spec-required 'Los mensajes de contexto deben estar entre 3 y 50'.
